title: Make one home upkeep routine easy to repeat

sections.title: Understand the distinction
sections.body: Upkeep combines readiness, condition and stock. A reset restores a known usable state; an inspection asks whether that state is still suitable; an inventory helps avoid missing or excessive supplies. A reminder does not prove any of them occurred.

sections.title: Complete fictional practice material
sections.body: Fictional bag station: two reusable bags are owned. A is clean and intact; B has a torn handle and is set aside, not counted ready. The household wants one ready bag at the reachable hook before each planned shop; both residents approve the hook. No new purchase is needed now. The next inspection is after use or visible damage, not an assumption of permanent condition.

sections.title: Work through the supplied case
sections.body: Plan one reversible readiness change and record ready, unavailable and unknown stock separately. Specify a reset trigger and a check that would stop counting a bag as ready.

sections.title: Try a different case before checking
sections.body: A shelf contains three containers, one cracked and one lent out. How many usable containers are presently available there?

checks.title: Compare reasoning and review the supplied result
checks.body: Place A on the agreed hook; B remains unavailable until appropriately repaired or retired. Later fiction: A is used but left elsewhere, so the next departure has zero bags at the station despite owning two. Partial: inventory count without condition/location. Incorrect: count B ready or buy more solely because reset failed. Progress to one other safe household supply by setting a use-based minimum, condition check and responsible replenishment route.
criteria: Reset and inspection are distinct performed actions

checks.title: Check the changed case
checks.body: One, under the stated condition and location facts. Ownership, stock, safe usability and readiness are different counts; keep the paper exercise separate from an actual inspection of your belongings.
criteria: Reset and inspection are distinct performed actions
